findings.finding: Political weighting adjusts sample composition; results depend on reference distributions and accuracy of recalled past votes. Weighting can reduce some composition errors without eliminating nonresponse, measurement or likely-voter error. Do not assign an accuracy score solely from poll sponsor or cost.

places: Probability sample mathematical illustration; no jurisdiction-specific law
findings.measure: derived 95-percent simple random sample half-width at p=.5, percentage points
findings.spread: p in [0,1] gives half-width [0, 1.96*sqrt(.25/n)*100]; complex design can be larger
findings.basis: Own binomial standard-error calculation; survey sampling background from Pew FAQ. These sample sizes are illustrations, not observed typical poll sizes. No finite-population correction. A two-candidate margin has approximately twice the candidate-share half-width; empirical election errors include additional biases.

gaps.finding: No matched outcome panel establishing amateur/internal/professional error, sponsor lean, cost relationship or local polling frequency. Pure sampling half-width is a sourced-method illustration, not a best empirical total-error estimate.
